summary: Built a NAVIGATION-REACH HARNESS (tools/libretro/trace-maze.ts `navreach`) that cold-boots a fresh party into dungeon level 0 and drives GENUINE forward moves up the entry corridor on the PATCHED trace core, reading the party DGROUP after each key to confirm the step took. DECISIVE RESULT: a real party MOVE re-runs the engine BUILD loop — the span COUNT [0x50ce] changes value on every cell step (gy 118->119->120->121 : spanCount 7->4->3->1), which a poke-recompose never produced (pokeview = 0 build-loop writes). This is the unblock the prior passes converged on: only a real move re-runs the build loop. The harness captures each NEW cell's framebuffer as a committed-format .idx.gz (the same EGA-index format as maze-corridor); the gx127 gy121 f0 capture (the documented fountain-column view) is committed as tools/parity/fixtures/engine/maze-fountain.idx.gz and its viewport matches the committed maze-corridor fixture at 99.99%. HONEST LIMITS: a free-roam navigateTo(arbitrary gx,gy,facing) is NOT achievable on the patched core — the scripted gate-entry walk consumes ENTER/UP as forward steps but holds the TURN keys (left/right) LOCKED for the entire entry corridor, so the party can only walk the gx127 column NORTH, never turn. The committed maze states that WOULD give a turnable free-roam frame do NOT unserialize on the patched core (`err unser`, DBPSerialize layout divergence). And the span-list write-watch [0x50d0] / DGROUP-wide [0x5000..0x5400] logs ZERO writes even on a real move whose span count DID change — so the wwatch cannot be used to trap the BUILD-loop emit stores in this configuration (a tracer limitation). The fallback the task spec anticipated was delivered: 4 fresh real-move build-loop captures (gy118..121) + the build-loop-re-runs confirmation.

findings.claim: A genuine party MOVE (real ENTER/UP forward step) re-runs the wmaze BUILD loop: the span COUNT at DGROUP [0x50ce] changes value on every cell change. Cold-boot drive lands at gx127 gy118 f0 (game_state 5); successive forward steps gy 118->119->120->121 carry spanCount 7->4->3->1. A poke-recompose (pokeview) produced 0 build-loop writes for the same kind of view — confirming the long-standing diagnosis that poke+recompose replays a cached span list while only a real move rebuilds it.

evidence.address: DGROUP [0x50ce] span count, [0x4fa2] gy, [0x4fa4] gx, [0x363a] game_state
evidence.details: tools/libretro/trace-maze.ts navreach. landed base=0xffa0 gs=5 gx=127 gy=118 f=0 cellA=2 cellB=7 sp=7 (region-0 mapping cellA=gy-116, cellB=gx-120 verified). move_log: enter gy118->119 sp7->4 moved=true spanCountChanged=true; gy119->120 sp4->3; gy120->121 sp3->1. build_loop_reran_on_real_move=true.

findings.claim: Cold-boot driveToMaze (3 ADD-PARTY-MEMBER + START NEW GAME + 6 ENTER-walk) lands the party at gx127 gy118 facing0 in game_state 5 — NOT gy121 as an older note recorded. The first arrow-controllable free-roam frame is documented as gy121, but on the patched trace core the party reaches gy121 only via the scripted gate-entry forward walk (ENTER/UP), and turns remain locked the whole way (see turn-lock finding).

evidence.details: landed gx127 gy118 f0 gs5; region-0 base gx120 gy116 so cellA=2 cellB=7. The entry-narration screen 'APPROACHING THE GATE WITH CONFIDENCE...' is up at landing (eyeballed /tmp framebuffer); the closed gem-grid portcullis is directly ahead.

findings.claim: During the scripted gate-entry walk, ENTER/UP advance the party NORTH up the gx127 column (gy 118->121) — these ARE genuine build-loop forward moves — but the TURN keys (left/right) are LOCKED: pressing left/right never changes facing [0x4f9a] anywhere on the entry corridor, even after the party reaches gy121 with game_state 5 and a long input-free settle. So a free-roam navigateTo(arbitrary cell, arbitrary facing) is unreachable from a cold boot on the patched core; only forward travel up the entry column is possible. This is consistent with the memory note that dosbox-pure's empty-magicword entry is the degenerate FAIL path (magicword SUCCESS = the animated entry that hands off to free-roam).

evidence.details: Across 5 cold-boot attempts driving to gy121 gs5 then probing LEFT: facing stayed 0 every time (turn-lock probe in navreach.json: LEFT f0->f0). Forward ENTER/UP DID move the party (gy advanced + spanCount changed). A monster encounter (game_state 12/13) also frequently fires at gy121 mid-walk, an additional non-deterministic obstruction.

findings.claim: The committed maze serialize-states (test-fixtures/states/maze-corridor.state.gz — the turnable gy121 free-roam base the nightly-core view-cases capture replays from) do NOT unserialize on the PATCHED trace core: HostClient.unserialize returns `err unser`. So the view-cases base-replay navigation pattern (which DOES give turnable free-roam on the nightly core) is unavailable for build-loop tracing on the patched core. This is the DBPSerialize layout divergence between the patched and nightly cores noted in maze-piece-inventory.json.

evidence.details: gunzip maze-corridor.state.gz -> c.unserialize -> `unserialize: err unser`. The nightly core unserializes the same file fine (capture-maze-view-cases.ts uses it as its base).

findings.claim: The build-loop emit stores are NOT observable via the patched core's memory write-watch in this configuration. Arming wwatch on the span-list region [0x50d0..+0x150], the slot array [0x5220..+0x20], and a DGROUP-wide window [0x5000..0x5400] across a REAL forward move whose span count [0x50ce] DEMONSTRABLY changed value logged ZERO writes. The store that changed [0x50ce] happened (the value differs before/after) but the wwatch did not record it — so the depthemit/buildwatch approach of trapping span_append stores to pin the shape-code->placement-index law remains blocked on the patched core, even with a genuine build-loop re-run.

evidence.details: Per-move: arm wwatch, press ENTER, drain. On moves where [0x50ce] changed (7->4, 4->3, 3->1 etc.) the drained write count was 0 for all three watched regions. The value-change proves the write occurred; the empty drain proves the wwatch missed it.

findings.claim: EXTENDED to `dectrace` (tools/libretro/trace-maze.ts): the INSTRUCTION-trace approach the prior unresolved note called for WORKS on a real-move frame. The trick the wwatch note missed: the SPAN-LIST write-watch [0x50d0] logs 0, but the COMPOSE-PAGE write-watch [0x41820] IS observable, and its OR plane-store cluster recovers the relocated ega.drv OR-blit base PER RUN (recoverOrBase -> 0x6ba10 on the cold-boot heap). With the base resolved, an instruction trace at the OR-blit ARG point (base+0xaad, ebx=arg0c=placement index) over each genuine forward step captures the full per-move emitted placement-index SET (the build loop re-ran: spanCount 7->4->3->1). dectrace drove gy118->121 and captured View A (gy120) and View B (gy121=maze-corridor) emit sets on real moves. RESULT: the gy121 set EQUALS generateCallist byte-for-byte; the gx126 fountain emits NO separate decoration index (it is the side-wall surface). See maze-decoration-generation.json dectrace-instruction-trace-on-real-move + slot-face-attribution-fix.

evidence.address: OR-blit base+0xaad (arg0c=placement index); compose-page [0x41820] plane-store cluster for base recovery
evidence.details: tools/libretro/trace-maze.ts `dectrace` -> /tmp/wiz6-dectrace.json. The span-list wwatch still logs 0 (the documented blindness), but the compose-page wwatch + the instruction trace at the OR ARG point succeed where the span-list trap failed. Head-on fountain nav (turn to gx126 facing north) remained blocked this run (LEFT consumed as a forward step — the entry-walk turn-lock is non-deterministic).

unresolved: A turnable free-roam navigateTo on the patched core is STILL flaky: the scripted entry walk consumes turn keys as forward steps NON-DETERMINISTICALLY (navreach saw LEFT turn once at gy121; the dectrace run had LEFT consumed as forward). So a reliable head-on decorated-cell view (e.g. gx126 facing north for the fountain's FRONT face) needs the magicword SUCCESS entry path or a patched-core turnable serialize-state.

RESOLVED for the decoration question: the build-loop emit law no longer needs the span-list write-watch — the dectrace instruction trace at the OR-blit ARG point (via the observable compose-page base recovery) captures the emitted placement indices on a real move. See dectrace-extension-real-move-instruction-trace.
